title: Going Concern Evaluation
exam_relevance: HIGHLY TESTED - Expect 4-6 questions on CPA AUD exam about going concern indicators, evaluation period, auditor procedures, management's assessment, mitigating factors, and reporting requirements. Understanding going concern is critical for both audit work and reporting.
learning_objectives: Understand the going concern assumption in accounting
Know the auditor's responsibility to evaluate going concern
Identify conditions and events that may indicate substantial doubt
Understand the evaluation period (one year from FS date)
Know required auditor procedures when indicators exist
Evaluate management's plans to mitigate going concern issues
Understand reporting requirements when substantial doubt exists
Know the emphasis-of-matter paragraph requirements for going concern

introduction.going_concern_assumption: Financial statements are prepared under the GOING CONCERN assumption - that the entity will continue in existence for the foreseeable future and will be able to realize assets and discharge liabilities in the normal course of business.
introduction.importance: If an entity is NOT a going concern (will likely cease operations), the financial statements may require significant adjustments (assets may need to be written down to liquidation values, liabilities may need to be reclassified as current).
introduction.auditor_responsibility: The auditor must evaluate whether there is substantial doubt about the entity's ability to continue as a going concern for a reasonable period of time.
introduction.key_standard: AU-C Section 570 (The Auditor's Consideration of an Entity's Ability to Continue as a Going Concern) provides the primary guidance.
introduction.exam_importance: Going concern is heavily tested. Know the indicators, evaluation period (one year), mitigating factors, and reporting requirements (emphasis-of-matter paragraph).

going_concern_defined.definition: An entity is considered a going concern when it can continue operations and meet its obligations for a reasonable period of time.

reasonable_period.definition: A period not to exceed ONE YEAR from the DATE OF THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
reasonable_period.example: For December 31, 2024 financial statements, evaluation period is through December 31, 2025
reasonable_period.key_point: ONE YEAR from the FS DATE (not from the audit report date or date of auditor's evaluation)
reasonable_period.exam_emphasis: The one-year period from FS date is heavily tested. Questions will ask about the evaluation period.

substantial_doubt.definition: Substantial doubt exists when there is a reasonable possibility that the entity will be unable to meet its obligations as they become due within one year from the financial statement date.
substantial_doubt.threshold: Not just 'possible' but 'reasonably possible' - more than remote but less than probable
substantial_doubt.effects_considered: Consider effects of conditions/events IN AGGREGATE (multiple issues together may create substantial doubt even if individually they wouldn't)

conditions_and_events_indicating_going_c.description: Certain conditions and events may indicate substantial doubt about going concern. Auditors must be alert to these indicators.

negative_financial_trends: Working capital deficiencies (current liabilities exceed current assets)
Adverse key financial ratios (low current ratio, high debt-to-equity, declining profitability)
Negative net worth or stockholders' deficit
other_financial_difficulties: Default on loan or debt covenants
Arrearages in dividends (preferred dividends not paid)
Denial of usual trade credit from suppliers
Need to seek new sources or methods of financing
Inability to obtain financing for essential new product development
internal_matters: Substantial dependence on success of particular project
external_matters: Legal proceedings that may jeopardize entity's ability to operate
Legislation or regulatory matters that may threaten operations
Loss of principal customer or supplier
Loss of key franchise, license, or patent

conditions_and_events_indicating_going_c.exam_strategy: Questions may describe entity's situation and ask whether going concern issues exist. Look for negative financial indicators (losses, deficits, defaults) and external threats.

auditor_evaluation_procedures.description: The auditor's evaluation of going concern is integrated throughout the audit. It's not a separate procedure but rather ongoing consideration.
procedures_in_planning_and_risk_assessme: Consider during risk assessment whether conditions indicate possible going concern issues
Inquire of management about their assessment of going concern
Review management's plans for dealing with financial difficulties
Consider results of analytical procedures (trends, ratios) that might indicate issues

procedures_when_indicators_exist.description: If conditions or events indicate possible going concern issues, auditor must perform ADDITIONAL procedures:

required_procedures.details: Obtain information about management's plans to mitigate the going concern issues. Evaluate whether plans are feasible and likely to be effective.
required_procedures.examples: Plans to sell assets, restructure debt, reduce/delay expenditures, increase equity

required_procedures.procedure: Obtain information about management's ABILITY TO IMPLEMENT plans
required_procedures.details: Assess whether management has capability to execute the plans
required_procedures.considerations: Availability of financing, binding commitments for asset sales, feasibility of cost reductions

required_procedures.procedure: Gather evidence about the EFFECTIVENESS of plans
required_procedures.details: Obtain evidence supporting that plans will mitigate the conditions
required_procedures.examples: Letters of intent from potential purchasers, commitment letters from lenders, detailed cost reduction analysis

required_procedures.details: Review minutes of board meetings, stockholder meetings, committees
required_procedures.purpose: Identify discussions about financial difficulties and actions taken

required_procedures.details: Discuss litigation, claims, assessments that could affect going concern
required_procedures.attorney_letter: Attorney's letter may provide information about threats to operations

required_procedures.details: Confirm arrangements for financial support, debt restructuring
required_procedures.purpose: Verify that financing plans are real and achievable

required_procedures.details: Consider events after balance sheet date that may affect going concern assessment
required_procedures.examples: Subsequent financing obtained, subsequent defaults, loss of major customer after year-end

required_procedures.details: Determine if entity is in compliance or has obtained waivers
required_procedures.impact: Covenant violations may accelerate debt maturity, creating liquidity crisis

required_procedures.procedure: Review ENTITY'S PROCEDURES for identifying going concern issues
required_procedures.details: Understand management's process for monitoring going concern
required_procedures.assessment: Does management have effective process for identifying risks?

written_representations.requirement: If substantial doubt exists, obtain WRITTEN REPRESENTATIONS from management about:
representations: Management's plans to mitigate the effects of conditions/events
written_representations.exam_note: Written representations are required when substantial doubt exists

management_plans_and_mitigating_factors.description: When evaluating going concern, auditor must consider management's PLANS to address the issues. Effective plans may alleviate substantial doubt.

plans_to_dispose_of_assets.description: Plans to sell assets to raise cash
plans_to_dispose_of_assets.examples: Sell non-core business units, sell real estate, sell investments or other assets
auditor_considerations: Is there binding commitment to purchase? Or just management's intent?
What is net realizable value? Is it sufficient?
Is sale feasible in the timeframe needed?
Will proceeds be sufficient to address the issues?
plans_to_dispose_of_assets.strength: Binding purchase commitment with adequate price = strong mitigation. Just 'plan to sell' = weak.

plans_to_borrow_or_restructure_debt.description: Plans to obtain financing or restructure existing debt
plans_to_borrow_or_restructure_debt.examples: Obtain new loans, refinance debt, extend payment terms, convert debt to equity
auditor_considerations: Is there commitment letter from lender? Or just management's intent to seek financing?
What are terms of new financing? Are they acceptable?
Is entity creditworthy? Will lenders actually provide financing?
For debt restructuring, have creditors agreed?
plans_to_borrow_or_restructure_debt.strength: Executed term sheet or commitment letter = strong. Just 'planning to seek financing' = weak.

plans_to_reduce_or_delay_expenditures.description: Plans to reduce costs or defer capital expenditures
plans_to_reduce_or_delay_expenditures.examples: Reduce R&D spending, defer equipment purchases, reduce payroll, cut discretionary expenses
auditor_considerations: Will cost reductions harm business long-term?
plans_to_reduce_or_delay_expenditures.strength: Specific, achievable cost cuts = moderate strength. Vague plans = weak.

plans_to_increase_ownership_equity.examples: Issue new stock, bring in new investors, obtain capital contributions from owners
auditor_considerations: Do investors have commitment to invest?
Is company attractive to investors given financial condition?
What are terms? Are they acceptable?
Is there market for the securities?
plans_to_increase_ownership_equity.strength: Binding commitment from investors = strong. Just 'plan to seek investors' = weak.

auditor_must_assess: Whether plans are FEASIBLE (can they realistically be implemented?)
Whether plans will be EFFECTIVE (will they solve the going concern issue?)
Whether plans are within management's CONTROL
Whether plans can be implemented in TIMEFRAME needed (within one year)
evaluating_effectiveness_of_plans.evidence_needed: Auditor must obtain evidence supporting the plans - not just accept management's assertions. Need commitment letters, binding agreements, detailed analysis, etc.
evaluating_effectiveness_of_plans.prospective_financial_information: Management may prepare cash flow forecasts to demonstrate that plans will work. Auditor should evaluate reasonableness of assumptions.

alleviating_substantial_doubt.if_plans_sufficient: If management's plans are feasible and effective such that substantial doubt is ALLEVIATED:
alleviating_substantial_doubt.outcome: NO substantial doubt exists. Auditor issues UNMODIFIED opinion with NO emphasis-of-matter paragraph.
alleviating_substantial_doubt.if_plans_insufficient: If plans are not sufficient to alleviate substantial doubt:
alleviating_substantial_doubt.outcome: Substantial doubt EXISTS. Auditor issues unmodified opinion but MUST include EMPHASIS-OF-MATTER paragraph describing the substantial doubt.

management_plans_and_mitigating_factors.exam_emphasis: Management plans must be FEASIBLE and EFFECTIVE to alleviate doubt. Binding commitments and executed agreements are strong evidence. Vague plans or intent are weak. This is heavily tested.

reporting_requirements.description: Reporting depends on whether substantial doubt exists and whether FS disclosures are adequate.

scenario_1_no_substantial_doubt.situation: No conditions indicating going concern issues, OR issues exist but management's plans alleviate substantial doubt
scenario_1_no_substantial_doubt.fs_disclosures: No special disclosures required in FS (though management may choose to disclose)
scenario_1_no_substantial_doubt.exam_note: If no substantial doubt (or alleviated), standard unmodified opinion - no modification needed

scenario_2_substantial_doubt_adequate_di.situation: Substantial doubt exists AND FS include adequate disclosure
scenario_2_substantial_doubt_adequate_di.auditor_report: UNMODIFIED opinion with REQUIRED EMPHASIS-OF-MATTER paragraph

emphasis_paragraph_requirements.heading: Must use heading: 'Substantial Doubt About the Entity's Ability to Continue as a Going Concern'
content_must_include: Reference to NOTE in FS that describes the principal conditions/events giving rise to substantial doubt
Reference to NOTE that describes management's evaluation of significance and management's plans
Statement that auditor's opinion is NOT MODIFIED with respect to the matter
emphasis_paragraph_requirements.example_wording: 'The accompanying financial statements have been prepared assuming that the Company will continue as a going concern. As discussed in Note X to the financial statements, the Company has suffered recurring losses from operations and has a net capital deficiency that raise substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern. Management's evaluation of the events and conditions and management's plans regarding these matters are also described in Note X. The financial statements do not include any adjustments that might result from the outcome of this uncertainty. Our opinion is not modified with respect to this matter.'

key_points.opinion_unmodified: The opinion itself is still UNMODIFIED - the emphasis paragraph does NOT modify the opinion
key_points.always_required: Emphasis paragraph is REQUIRED when substantial doubt exists, even if disclosure is adequate (recent change - used to be optional if adequately disclosed)
key_points.reference_to_note: Must reference the NOTE where management discloses the going concern issue

scenario_2_substantial_doubt_adequate_di.exam_critical: When substantial doubt exists with adequate disclosure, issue unmodified opinion + REQUIRED emphasis-of-matter paragraph. This is heavily tested.

scenario_3_substantial_doubt_inadequate_.situation: Substantial doubt exists but FS do NOT adequately disclose the conditions/events
scenario_3_substantial_doubt_inadequate_.auditor_report: QUALIFIED or ADVERSE opinion for GAAP departure (inadequate disclosure)
scenario_3_substantial_doubt_inadequate_.rationale: Failing to disclose going concern issues when substantial doubt exists is a departure from GAAP (inadequate disclosure). This requires modified opinion.

opinion_type.if_material_and_pervasive: ADVERSE opinion (going concern issues are usually pervasive)

scenario_3_substantial_doubt_inadequate_.also_include: In addition to qualified/adverse opinion, should ALSO include emphasis-of-matter paragraph describing the going concern issue
scenario_3_substantial_doubt_inadequate_.exam_note: Inadequate disclosure = GAAP departure = qualified or adverse opinion. This is different from adequate disclosure scenario.

exam_summary_table.substantial_doubt_inadequate_disclosure: Qualified or adverse opinion (GAAP departure) + emphasis paragraph

fs_disclosure_requirements.description: When substantial doubt about going concern exists, management must include disclosures in the financial statements.
required_disclosures_by_management: Principal conditions and events that gave rise to substantial doubt
Management's evaluation of the significance of those conditions/events
Management's PLANS to mitigate the conditions (if any)
Statement that substantial doubt exists (may or may not be explicitly stated depending on circumstances)
fs_disclosure_requirements.adequate_disclosure_assessment: Auditor must assess whether management's disclosures are ADEQUATE. If inadequate, it's a GAAP departure requiring modified opinion.
fs_disclosure_requirements.exam_note: Management is responsible for disclosure. Auditor assesses adequacy. Inadequate = GAAP departure.

liquidation_basis.situation: If entity is in liquidation or plans to liquidate
liquidation_basis.accounting: FS should be prepared on LIQUIDATION basis (not going concern basis) - assets at net realizable value, liabilities at settlement amounts
liquidation_basis.auditor_consideration: Auditor evaluates whether liquidation basis is appropriate and properly applied

subsequent_events.consideration: Events occurring AFTER the balance sheet date but BEFORE the audit report date may affect going concern assessment
subsequent_events.examples: Subsequent financing obtained, subsequent loss of major customer, subsequent defaults
subsequent_events.impact: May alleviate or worsen going concern assessment

use_of_estimates.uncertainty: Going concern involves significant uncertainty and management judgment
use_of_estimates.auditor_role: Auditor evaluates reasonableness of assumptions and judgments, but ultimate outcome is uncertain

practice_problems.question:
ABC Company has the following situation as of December 31, 2024:
- Recurring operating losses for the past three years
- Working capital deficit of $5 million
- Default on loan covenant (debt-to-equity ratio exceeded permitted level)
- Management has obtained a commitment letter from a lender to refinance the defaulted debt with more favorable terms, which would cure the covenant violation

Required:
1. What is the evaluation period for going concern?
2. Do conditions exist that may indicate substantial doubt?
3. Does substantial doubt exist after considering management's plans?
4. What type of audit opinion should be issued, and is an emphasis-of-matter paragraph required?

part_1_evaluation_period.answer: ONE YEAR from December 31, 2024 = through December 31, 2025
part_1_evaluation_period.rule: Evaluation period is one year from the FINANCIAL STATEMENT DATE
part_1_evaluation_period.not_from: Not one year from audit report date or date of evaluation - from FS date

part_2_indicators_exist.answer: YES, multiple conditions indicate potential going concern issues
indicators_present: Working capital deficit (current liabilities exceed current assets)
part_2_indicators_exist.conclusion: These conditions, in aggregate, raise concern about entity's ability to meet obligations over the next year. Auditor must perform additional procedures to evaluate going concern.

part_3_substantial_doubt_exists.analysis: Management has obtained a COMMITMENT LETTER from lender to refinance debt with favorable terms. This is a FEASIBLE and EFFECTIVE plan.
part_3_substantial_doubt_exists.commitment_letter: Commitment letter is strong evidence - it's a binding commitment from lender, not just management's intent to seek financing.
part_3_substantial_doubt_exists.will_it_work: Refinancing would cure the covenant violation and presumably improve liquidity (more favorable terms).
part_3_substantial_doubt_exists.other_issues: However, operating losses and working capital deficit still exist. Refinancing helps with immediate liquidity but doesn't address underlying operational issues.
part_3_substantial_doubt_exists.scenario_A: If refinancing is sufficient to meet obligations for one year despite operational issues, substantial doubt may be ALLEVIATED.
part_3_substantial_doubt_exists.scenario_B: If operating losses are so severe that even with refinancing the company cannot meet obligations, substantial doubt still EXISTS.
part_3_substantial_doubt_exists.exam_approach: With commitment letter (strong evidence of feasible plan), likely conclude substantial doubt is ALLEVIATED unless question indicates ongoing problems are too severe.

if_doubt_alleviated.reasoning: If management's plans alleviate substantial doubt, going concern issue is resolved. Standard unmodified opinion with no special reporting.

if_doubt_still_exists.paragraph_heading: 'Substantial Doubt About the Entity's Ability to Continue as a Going Concern'
if_doubt_still_exists.paragraph_content: References FS note describing conditions (losses, deficit, default), management's evaluation, and management's plans (refinancing commitment). States opinion not modified.
if_doubt_still_exists.reasoning: Substantial doubt exists but FS adequately disclose = unmodified opinion with required emphasis paragraph

key_exam_points: Commitment letter is strong evidence - it's a binding commitment, which makes the plan feasible
Must consider if plan is effective - does refinancing solve the problem for one year?
If doubt alleviated = no emphasis paragraph. If doubt exists = required emphasis paragraph (assuming adequate disclosure)

tip_1_evaluation_period.description: ONE YEAR from financial statement DATE
tip_1_evaluation_period.exam_question: Questions frequently ask about the evaluation period
tip_1_evaluation_period.answer: One year from FS date (not report date, not evaluation date)

tip_2_indicators.description: Know common indicators of going concern issues
tip_2_indicators.most_common: Recurring losses, working capital deficiency, negative cash flows, debt defaults, net worth deficit
tip_2_indicators.exam_strategy: Question will describe company's situation - look for these red flags

tip_3_management_plans.description: Management plans must be FEASIBLE and EFFECTIVE
tip_3_management_plans.strong_evidence: Binding commitments, executed agreements, commitment letters
tip_3_management_plans.weak_evidence: Just 'plans to' or 'intends to' without binding agreements
tip_3_management_plans.exam_question: Question describes management's plans - assess if they're feasible and will work

tip_4_reporting_three_scenarios.exam_critical: The emphasis paragraph is REQUIRED when substantial doubt exists (even with adequate disclosure)

tip_5_emphasis_paragraph_always_required.description: Recent change - emphasis paragraph is now ALWAYS required when substantial doubt exists
tip_5_emphasis_paragraph_always_required.old_rule: Used to be optional if adequate disclosure
tip_5_emphasis_paragraph_always_required.new_rule: Now REQUIRED even if adequately disclosed
tip_5_emphasis_paragraph_always_required.exam_importance: This is heavily tested - don't forget the emphasis paragraph

tip_6_opinion_is_unmodified.description: When substantial doubt exists with adequate disclosure, opinion is UNMODIFIED
tip_6_opinion_is_unmodified.trap: Don't think substantial doubt requires modified opinion - it doesn't (if disclosure adequate)
tip_6_opinion_is_unmodified.modified_only_if: Only modify opinion if disclosure is INADEQUATE (GAAP departure)
tip_6_opinion_is_unmodified.emphasis_paragraph: Emphasis paragraph highlights going concern but doesn't modify the opinion

tip_7_alleviating_doubt.description: Effective plans can alleviate substantial doubt
tip_7_alleviating_doubt.if_alleviated: No emphasis paragraph needed - back to standard unmodified opinion
tip_7_alleviating_doubt.strength_of_plans: Binding commitments are key - 'plans to' is weak, commitment letter is strong
tip_7_alleviating_doubt.exam_scenario: Question gives you indicators BUT also gives you strong mitigating plan - doubt may be alleviated

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: What is the going concern evaluation period?
Describe company situation - does substantial doubt exist?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Look for indicators (losses, deficits, defaults). Consider if management plans alleviate doubt.

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: Substantial doubt exists and FS adequately disclose - what opinion?
Describe management's plans - are they sufficient?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Are plans feasible (binding commitments?) and effective (will they work?)?
Reference to FS note, describes conditions/plans, states opinion not modified

memorization_aids.evaluation_period: One year from FS date (not report date)
memorization_aids.reporting_scenarios: No doubt = standard. Doubt + adequate = emphasis. Doubt + inadequate = modified opinion.
memorization_aids.emphasis_required: Substantial Doubt? → Emphasis Required (even if adequate disclosure)

key_concepts: Going concern = entity can continue operations and meet obligations for one year from FS date
Evaluation period = ONE YEAR from FINANCIAL STATEMENT DATE
Substantial doubt = reasonable possibility entity cannot meet obligations within one year
Common indicators: recurring losses, working capital deficiency, defaults, negative cash flows
Management plans must be FEASIBLE and EFFECTIVE to alleviate doubt
Binding commitments (commitment letters, executed agreements) are strong evidence of feasibility
Three reporting scenarios: (1) No doubt = standard, (2) Doubt + adequate disclosure = unmodified + emphasis, (3) Doubt + inadequate = modified opinion
Emphasis-of-matter paragraph is REQUIRED when substantial doubt exists (even if adequately disclosed)
Emphasis paragraph placed after Opinion section, references FS note, states opinion not modified
Inadequate disclosure = GAAP departure = qualified or adverse opinion
critical_for_exam: One year evaluation period from FS date
Management plans must be feasible and effective - binding commitments key
Three reporting scenarios and which opinion/paragraph for each
Emphasis paragraph is REQUIRED when substantial doubt exists
Opinion is UNMODIFIED when doubt exists but disclosure adequate
Modified opinion only if disclosure INADEQUATE
common_mistakes: Thinking evaluation period is from report date (it's from FS date)
Thinking emphasis paragraph is optional when adequately disclosed (it's REQUIRED)
Thinking substantial doubt automatically requires modified opinion (only if inadequate disclosure)
Not recognizing that binding commitments make plans feasible (commitment letter is strong)
Forgetting to assess if plans are both feasible AND effective
Not placing emphasis paragraph in correct location (goes after Opinion section)

AU-C Section 705: Modifications to the Opinion in the Independent Auditor's Report
